text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: Degraded multi-GPU collectives observed on prod-gpu-pool-7 affecting TP4 pipeline jobs. Symptoms: intermittent NCCL TIMEOUT / RING FORMATION failures across 3-5 ranks. Rate ~10% of active runs. Auto-alert triggered at 01:23 UTC.

jamie (oncall): acked. I'm grabbing logs and starting triage. Can someone check kv-cache and node metrics?

leena (eng-runtime): seeing a burst of KV cache evictions coincident with spikes in network retransmits on gpu-7a/7b. Quick log snippet:
```
[2024-10-05T01:22:58Z] nccl: ERROR TIMEOUT, rank 3 -> rendezvous failed after 120s
[2024-10-05T01:23:00Z] cuda: Xid 79 (GPU hang), driver reset triggered on gpu-7a
[2024-10-05T01:23:05Z] runtime: communicator cleanup, leader flip attempt
```
This smells like a transient device hang combined with collectives not recovering.

priya (sre): confirmed node-level kernel messages include repeated `nv_peer_memory` warnings and a short period of high PCIe retrains. I'm going to cordon node gpu-7a and restart the container runtime on the affected pods. Planning: cordon -> drain -> restart containerd on node -> uncordon. Minimal blast radius.

oliver (ml-infra): suggested live mitigation: route new TP/PP jobs away from prod-gpu-pool-7 and enable fallback to single-GPU variant for streaming customers. We can flip smart routing with a short rollout:
```
# route update to prefer fallback model for affected shard
redwood-cli route update --pool prod-gpu-pool-7 --set fallback_model=small-gpt --weight 1.0 --drain 30s
# scale down concurrent TP4 jobs to reduce rendezvous pressure
redwood-cli jobs scale --selector=tp-version=4 --concurrency 50%
```
This should reduce new failures immediately.

sam (cust-succ): impacted customers flagged: Acme (batch inference) and BetaApps (low-latency streaming). Acme reported ~12 failed runs in last 30m, BetaApps metrics show increased tail latency. I'm prepping a short customer note to say we're investigating and routing traffic.

jamie (oncall): executing cordon+drain on gpu-7a now. ETA 8m. Will restart runtimes and keep node cordoned until we validate stable collectives. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

leena (eng-runtime): also increasing NCCL rendezvous timeout to 300s for the pool as a safety net while we investigate. Config change pushed: `nccl.rendezvous.timeout=300s` on pool config.

priya (sre): drain completed. Restarting container runtime -> issuing `systemctl restart containerd` on gpu-7a. Monitoring dmesg and NCCL logs.

incident-bot: automation: notifying on-call rotation and creating incident page: https://internal.redwood/incident/INC-20241005-1723456789

jamie (oncall): containerd restarted, rejoining node. Observing reduced Xid events but still occasional NCCL TIMEOUT at low rate (~1-2%). Keeping node cordoned for now.

oliver (ml-infra): rolled routing to fallback_model for new requests. Also enabling a temporary model-variant policy: prefer single-GPU variant for sessions with >1.5s setup variance.

leena (eng-runtime): ran `nccl-health-check` across ranks post-restart: allcollectives OK for 200 runs except one transient timeout we saw at 01:47 UTC. Logs point to rank 5 experiencing delayed heartbeat before rendezvous complete. Might be intermittent PCIe link flaps under high KV cache pressure.

sam (cust-succ): customer note sent to BetaApps and Acme: short heads-up + mitigation steps (routing/fallback). Keeping them updated.

jamie (oncall): handing off to next oncall (nora) in 30m. Key action items logged in incident doc:
- follow up on root cause (nv_peer_memory/kernel/drivers)
- run extended stress test across TP4 with KV cache stress profile
- evaluate persistent routing rule vs autoscaling for pool
- draft postmortem and customer impact timeline

nora (ops): taking over. Please @me on the incident doc and drop pointers to any stacks/commands executed. I'll coordinate a deeper hardware runbook and liaise with HW vendor if kernel traces point that way.

leena (eng-runtime): added notes: need to capture full /var/log/nvidia and `dmesg -T` from the window, and a copy of the NCCL debug logs with `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO` from one failed job for postmortem. Also propose throttling KV cache eviction watermark until we fix the root cause.

priya (sre): agreed. I'll schedule a follow-up 1-hour async postmortem and tag security for any customer-data checks (we did not see data plane compromise).

jamie (oncall): final status before handoff: degraded -> partial mitigation. New traffic routed away, node restarted, error rate down from ~10% to ~1-2%. Customers notified. Handoff to @nora for investigation and postmortem. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: incident state updated -> UNDER INVESTIGATION (mitigations applied). Escalation channel: #eng-runtime #incidents #customer-success

nora (ops): ack. I'll pick this up and open follow-up tickets for HW trace, KV cache tuning, and potential routing policy improvements.

leena (eng-runtime): adding a quick snippet to reproduce in staging under stress (for triage):
```
# run pipeline with forced kv-cache churn and small batch sizes to increase rendezvous frequency
redwood-cli job run --model tp4-gpt --batch 1 --kv-churn 1.5 --runs 1000 --region us-west2-staging
```
Please run ASAP.

sam (cust-succ): keeping customers updated. Will share incident doc link after postmortem is drafted.

nora (ops): taking ownership; marking as 'oncall handoff' in the incident doc. Will update timeline when we have full logs.

leena (eng-runtime): thanks everyone. Assigning follow-ups: ENG-RUNTIME -> root cause + fix, ML-INFRA -> routing and model fallback tuning, SRE -> node runbook and HW escalation.

jamie (oncall): handing off now. Good job team. :thumbsup:
